deities: Bale Miyan (Sufi saint; tomb shrine, not a Hindu deity)

history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. This is a Muslim dargah (tomb shrine of the Sufi saint Bale Miyan / Baley Miyan), reportedly built in 1194 by Qutb-ud-din Aibak, the first ruler of the Delhi Sultanate. It stands adjacent to the Chandi Devi Mandir near Nauchandi Ground, and the pairing is cited as a symbol of Hindu-Muslim unity. It is famous for the annual Urs festival with qawwali nights, held during the month-long Nauchandi Mela (opens on the second Sunday after Holi, roughly March-April).

town_description: Meerut, in western Uttar Pradesh about 70 km northeast of Delhi, is one of the NCR's largest cities - known as the 'Sports City of India' for its sports-goods industry - and is historically famous as the city where the 1857 uprising began.

travel.airport: Meerut Airport has limited services; the nearest major airport is Indira Gandhi International Airport, Delhi (~70-90 km)
travel.railway: Meerut City Junction is the nearest major station (~2-3 km from most city temples); the city has seven railway stations
travel.road: Well connected via NH-58 and the Delhi-Meerut Expressway; city buses, auto-rickshaws and taxis available

visitor_information.opening_hours: No published timings found; dargahs are generally open daily for ziyarat - verify
